main_text.p: pe gutturali aliqua vel Resch ) mutatur pathah in camez.
Secundò ה He mutat suum pathah in segol sequente ה vel ח heth.
ה He est etiam Adverbium interrogādi, & tunc habet -: hatephpathah, aut ante gutturalem & ante schevatam solum pathah, aut si gutturalis habeat camez, ה habet segol.
ו Vau serviens in principio est Conjunctio copulativa. Punctatur autem sic: Primò ו vau habet subjectū scheva, quod sequente litera schevata aut labiali, mutatur in schurec.
Secundò, ו vau quando parvas voces conjungit, mutat suum scheva in camez: ut וָךְ קח kach valech.
Tertiò ו vau convertit praeteritū, quando nullū aliud praecedit, in futurū, & tunc punctatur cum scheva: quod cum mutandum est, mutatur juxta regulas traditas.

page.notes: Hebrew words in the text: "ךְ קח" and "וָךְ" are as legible on the scan; the Hebrew in the fourth-to-last paragraph ("ו vau" forms and "ה He") is rendered with the Hebrew letters as printed. The Hebrew word after "ut" is partly illegible and may be transcribed imperfectly; the word "valech" is in Latin letters as printed. Lines 1 and 2 of the page are a continuation from the previous page. "Resch" is printed as a Hebrew letter with its Latin name. Some Hebrew letters within the text are small and may be misread; the transliterations "pathah", "segol", "camez", "schevata", "schurec" and "hatephpathah" are read as printed.
